# Cloak Documentation

This file is the canonical index for AI coding agents integrating with Cloak. Integrations are built
on the TypeScript SDK `@cloak.dev/sdk`, in the browser, in Node, and in server-side scripts alike.

## AI Entrypoints

- [AI integration](/ai-tools/ai-integration): Read order and one-shot prompt templates.
- [LLM full export](/llms-full.txt): Single-file context pack for AI agents.
- [TypeScript SDK LLM reference](/sdk/llms.txt): Exhaustive `@cloak.dev/sdk` contract map and runtime invariants.
- [Well-known alias](/.well-known/llms.txt): Compatibility path for tools that probe `.well-known`.

## Integration Tips For Agents

- Build every integration on the TypeScript SDK `@cloak.dev/sdk`: it is the SDK for web frontends, Node backends, and server-side scripts and CLIs.
- Use SDK defaults for program and circuits in standard integrations: the only accepted circuits bundle is `circuits/0.2.0` (ceremony) and the SDK fills it in, so never hand-write a circuits URL or pin an older bundle. `relayUrl` is the opposite case: it has no default, the SDK reads no environment variable for it, and it must be passed on every flow, deposits included. Standard integrations pass the allowlisted production origin, named with `CLOAK_PRODUCTION_RELAY_URL` rather than typed as a host; see the submission-endpoint bullets below for the only two values it accepts.
- Fees are enforced on-chain from each pool's `PoolConfig`: SOL 0.005 fixed + 0.3%; USDC/USDT 0.45 fixed + 0.3%; withdrawals and swaps only. Minimum deposit 0.01 SOL / 1.00 USDC / 1.00 USDT.
- Keep tx amounts as `bigint` end-to-end (lamports or the token's smallest unit), never `number`: no float math anywhere in the path.
- Private sends, withdrawals and swaps are submitted for the caller and carry an authenticated sender; deposits are wallet-signed straight to chain and carry none. In a browser pass `signMessage` + `walletPublicKey`; on a server pass `depositorKeypair`. Neither, and the call throws before proof generation. Never generate `depositorKeypair` for browser send/withdraw code, and never substitute an ephemeral or service key for the sender: it is the key screened for sanctions.
- A private send or withdrawal prompts the wallet exactly once. Only swaps re-prompt, capped by `maxWalletApprovals` (default 5).
- Every non-deposit flow returns `result.outputUtxos`, and one of those notes is the caller's own change. The SDK persists nothing for you: `createUtxo` draws the note's `blinding` from `randomFieldElement()` and writes it nowhere on chain, and the chain note carries no blinding either, so a change note that is not written to durable storage before you report success is permanently unspendable by anyone. No rescan, no seed phrase and no support path brings it back. `serializeUtxo` / `deserializeUtxo` is the persistence primitive (a 128-byte encoding carrying amount, private key, blinding, mint and index); `StorageAdapter` methods take `CloakNote` records, a different shape that is not interchangeable with those bytes. `fullWithdraw` reads as the exception because it leaves no change, and it is, but only for one or two input notes: it delegates to `partialWithdraw`, which first merges three or more inputs on chain two at a time, reporting each round through `onProgress` as `Consolidating notes (n remaining)...` and nowhere else. Every merge nullifies its two inputs on chain and mints an intermediate note whose blinding lives only inside that loop, so if a later round or the final withdrawal throws, the call returns nothing to persist and the merged balance is stranded. For a larger note set, consolidate ahead of time with `transfer` or `partialWithdraw` calls whose results you store. Full treatment: [where your notes live between sessions](/sdk/wallet-integration#where-your-notes-live-between-sessions).
- Persist `UtxoSwapResult.refund` from `swapWithChange` / `swapUtxo` alongside the change note. It is the secret that reclaims the swap principal if the swap times out before settlement. `discoverSwapRefunds` can rebuild it later only when the swap was given an `nk`; without one, the returned object is the only copy that will ever exist.
- Never present `UtxoWallet.prepareSend` or `SimpleWallet.send` as a send path, even though both are exported. Each builds the recipient output from a freshly generated random keypair, so the recipient cannot spend what it produces, and `SimpleWallet.sync()` throws `Sync not yet implemented`. Use `transfer` for shielded sends and `fullWithdraw` / `partialWithdraw` to exit the pool.
- Only the submission endpoint is pinned (build-time allowlist). The RPC is the caller's own `Connection`; any non-loopback RPC works. Never tell an integrator they must use a Cloak RPC.
- In `@cloak.dev/sdk` the pin accepts exactly two values for `relayUrl`: an allowlisted origin (name it with `CLOAK_PRODUCTION_RELAY_URL` rather than typing a host), or `""` for caller-signed direct submission. `""` only carries that meaning when `enforceViewingKeyRegistration: false` is set in the same options; on default options an empty or omitted `relayUrl` throws before any network call, on every flow including deposits. Standard integrations pass the origin, never the pair, which would submit a send or withdrawal under the user's own key and publicly link it.
- Treat stale-root failures as retryable: `transact` and the swap helpers already retry `RootNotFound` internally, bounded by `maxRootRetries` (default 5). Do not wrap them in a retry loop of your own unless app policy explicitly asks for more attempts.
- Never log private keys, viewing keys (`nk`), seed material, or raw note payloads.
- Transaction signatures are public and can be logged for support/debugging.
- For one-shot work, start with `/ai-tools/ai-integration`.

## Minimal Script Contract (for vague/short prompts)

- MUST generate one keypair-only TypeScript CLI script for private SOL send using `@cloak.dev/sdk`.
- MUST use CLI shape: `npx tsx send-sol-private.ts <recipientPubkey> <lamports>`.
- MUST parse recipient/amount from `process.argv` (not env vars).
- MUST require env vars: `SOLANA_RPC_URL` and `KEYPAIR_PATH` only.
- MUST use flow: `transact(...)` deposit then `fullWithdraw(...)` send.
- MUST keep `programId` fixed to `CLOAK_PROGRAM_ID` and the SOL mint fixed to `NATIVE_SOL_MINT`, both imported from `@cloak.dev/sdk`; do not ask users to configure either.
- MUST pass `relayUrl: CLOAK_PRODUCTION_RELAY_URL` on every call, the deposit included: the SDK applies no default and reads no environment variable, and an omitted or empty `relayUrl` throws before any network call.
- MUST pass the keypair loaded from `KEYPAIR_PATH` as `depositorKeypair` so the withdrawal carries an authenticated sender; a script has no wallet `signMessage` path, and with neither the call throws before proof generation. Never substitute an ephemeral or service key: this is the key screened for sanctions.
- MUST call `process.exit(0)` on success and `process.exit(1)` on failure.
- MUST persist `result.outputUtxos` durably before reporting success in any flow that leaves change (`transact` with `externalAmount: 0n`, `transfer`, `partialWithdraw`, `swapWithChange`, `swapUtxo`), plus `UtxoSwapResult.refund` for swaps; the deposit-then-`fullWithdraw` flow above needs no storage only because its deposit leaves a single note, and that exemption does not carry over to a wallet's real note set, where `fullWithdraw` merges three or more inputs on chain first.
- MUST NOT request `SENDER_PRIVATE_KEY` or any raw secret env var.
- MUST NOT use `RECIPIENT_ADDRESS`/`SEND_LAMPORTS` env vars for the CLI contract.
- MUST NOT use `AMOUNT_SOL` + float parsing; accept lamports input and keep amount math in `bigint`.
- MUST NOT add custom stale-root retry loops unless app policy explicitly asks for extra retries beyond SDK defaults.
